Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and the State.
2. This is an application for bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioners in apprehension of arrest for their alleged involvement in the offences 391-D/376(2)(n)/506/313/34 of IPC.
3. Learned counsel for the Petitioners submits that a false allegation has been lodged against the present Petitioners.
He further contended that there is discrepancy with regard to the date allegedly to have been mentioned in the FIR and the statement of the Informant, who is none but the mother of the victim.

Learned counsel also submitted that the discrepancies appear in the statement of the victim and the Informant being material to the // 2 // initiation of the case, the FIR lodged against the present Petitioners is stage managed.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the Informant, on the other hand vehemently opposed the contentions of the learned counsel for the Petitioners and submitted that the description of the FIR coupled with the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.PC clearly establishes the conduct of the Petitioner No.1 and the manner in which the victim has been subjected to the carnal act besides being harassed and threatened.

sentences.text: victim being ostracized in the society she was given in marriage but the Petitioner No.1 reached the in- law's house of the victim and revealed his relationship with her thereby brought a dissension in the in-law's family of the victim for which she was forced to leave her husband.
The Petitioner No.1 succeeded in blackmailing and harassing the victim and as such no leniency can be shown to the Petitioners in considering their anticipatory bail application.
He further submits that Petitioner No.2, the mother of Petitioner No.1 did not let the victim to enter into the house.

5. Keeping in view the submission of the parties, perusal of the FIR so also the statement of the victim recorded under section 164 of the CrPC, there appears substantial material to indict the conduct of the Petitioner No.1 as the manner in which she was subjected to the carnal act time and again and the fact that the victim submitted to the Petitioner was under duress and threat, the discrepancies pointed out by the learned counsel for the Petitioners in the FIR and the // 3 //
statement of the victim so also the statement of the Informant and her mother are the matters to be thrashed during the trial and the nature of allegations as emerged from the materials on record, the circumstances appearing, the seriousness and gravity of the offences, this court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioners.
Accordingly the prayer for bail stands rejected and the ABLAPL is dismissed.
